description: The writes through the clone in inputs/linked-counts-below-leaves, a header and a root that say 41 over leaves that hold more, which the freeze hazard, an undefined use, left in a committed file with no byte damaged. Since 274418f the original checks a leaf's count in every descent by rank, so a write whose rank runs past a leaf raises InvalidBTreeNode, where at 89da8e7 it panicked, or a get wrote past the leaf and committed. Each such write is here as a top-level op, so its transaction fails and the file is left as it was loaded. Then each kind of write once in a callback that handles the error, where what the write had written before its leaf check decides whether the transaction is poisoned (SCRIPT-FORMAT.md section 11). The clone's header is copied into the transaction first, so what each callback holds is the write's own. An append, a remove and a get write nothing before their leaf check, so the transaction commits there, and a port's bytes must agree. A slice writes before its leaf check, so its transaction is poisoned and isn't committed (finding 16): this is linked-counts-below-leaves-writes with what the port does there. Then, each in a database of its own, the positions next to the ones that raise, which succeed, so that a check made too early shows. tests/undefined/frozen-clone-linked-append and the wrappers frozen_clone_append and frozen_clone_remove reach the same kind of tree within one transaction, which stays an undefined use.
